content.text: The text reviews intestinal obstruction, especially intussusception, fecal impaction, strictures, adhesions, tumors, volvulus, and cancer. Acute obstruction causes sudden colicky pain, vomiting, distension, constipation, peritonitis, collapse, and possible gangrene; chronic obstruction develops gradually with constipation, alternating diarrhea, wasting, and eventual occlusion. Diagnosis relies on history, palpation, rectal examination, and distinguishing mechanical from functional disease. Older treatment emphasized opium, enemas, cautious reduction, and early laparotomy when strangulation persisted, while cancer treatment was largely palliative or surgical. Rectal diseases discussed include prolapse, polyps, hemorrhoids, fissures, ulcers, abscesses, fistulae, strictures, infections, and neurologic dysfunction. Intestinal parasites—including tapeworms, flukes, pinworms, and roundworms—are described with their life cycles, symptoms, treatment, and prevention. Sandra travelled to the kitchen. Daniel travelled to the bathroom.
